subject.title: [Feature]: Per-agent cost budget enforcement at the gateway level

question: Should OpenClaw implement per-agent spend-budget enforcement as a native gateway admission layer, expose a budget-capable plugin/admission API, or leave enforcement to external/provider controls?
rationale: The remaining work sets new config, provider dispatch policy, persistent accounting state, fallback behavior, and operator-facing status/doctor UX, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product boundary.

options.title: Native Gateway Admission
options.body: Add opt-in per-agent budgets in core with durable reservations/refunds, budget receipts, reset windows, status/doctor surfaces, and plugin observability hooks.

options.title: Plugin/API Boundary First
options.body: Extend the plugin/admission contract enough for budget systems to refuse model dispatch before spend while core stays limited to generic hooks and reporting.

options.title: External Controls Only
options.body: Document provider quotas, separate accounts, local proxies, and external budget systems as the supported path without adding core budget config.

recommendation.title: Native Gateway Admission
recommendation.body: Add opt-in per-agent budgets in core with durable reservations/refunds, budget receipts, reset windows, status/doctor surfaces, and plugin observability hooks.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest observed connection to the cost reporting implementation and prior product-boundary decisions around cost/budget scope.
